quantity: fraction of the remaining gap to mastery closed per practice opportunity
source: Corbett & Anderson (1995), Bayesian Knowledge Tracing; parameter defaults as shipped by pyBKT (Badrinath, Wang & Pardos, EDM 2021) and CMU's TutorShop.
reported: p(T), the probability that a skill moves to the mastered state per practice opportunity. Common EM initialisation is 0.10; TutorShop ships p_learn = 0.22; fitted values vary widely across skills.
model_quantity: alpha_i * E * F. Eq. 21's gain term is alpha * E * F * (1 - K), the same "close a fraction of the remaining gap" form as BKT's P(L_t+1) = P(L_t) + p(T) * (1 - P(L_t)), so the two are on one scale. E and F are the mean effort and effectiveness actually realised in the reference run, not their maxima.

quantity: fraction of knowledge retained after one year without practice
model_detail: one year at the break rate low 0.525, medium 0.382, high 0.217; at the term rate low 0.0759, medium 0.0212, high 0.0022
source: Custers, E. J. F. M. (2010). Long-term retention of basic science knowledge: a review study. Advances in Health Sciences Education 15(1), 109-128.
reported: Roughly two-thirds to three-quarters of taught knowledge is retained one year after instruction (25-35% lost), falling to somewhat below one half by the second year. Measured on classroom material without further instruction, which is the right comparison here: the lab forgetting curve for nonsense syllables is far steeper and does not describe taught content.
model_quantity: (1 - delta)^n, the eq. 21 decay compounded over a year of no practice. A16 makes delta a per-episode rate at `reference_episodes_per_week`, so a year is 52 * reference_episodes_per_week episode-equivalents at the term rate, or that times `break_decay_scale` at the break rate (D4). Both are reported; the break rate is the one the simulation ever actually applies over a long gap.

model_detail: support gap (eq. 26) at the §7.7 checkpoints, standardised by the SD of unaided accuracy
cite: Kulik & Fletcher (2016); Ma et al. (2014); VanLehn (2011)
source: Kulik, J. A. & Fletcher, J. D. (2016), Review of Educational Research 86(1), 42-78 (median effect 0.66, g about 0.62); Ma, W., Adesope, O. O., Nesbit, J. C. & Liu, Q. (2014), Journal of Educational Psychology 106(4), 901-918 (g about 0.35-0.44 depending on the comparison); VanLehn, K. (2011), Educational Psychologist 46(4), 197-221 (step-based tutoring about 0.76 against no tutoring).
reported: Standardised gain in test performance from tutoring support relative to unsupported instruction. The three meta-analyses disagree by more than a factor of two, so the range below is deliberately wide.
model_quantity: (supported accuracy - unaided accuracy) / SD(unaided accuracy) at the §7.7 checkpoints, where `supported` is one hint (support h = 1/3, A12). This is the model's own support gap (eq. 26) expressed as a standardised effect, which is what the meta-analyses report.

source: Rowland, C. A. (2014), Psychological Bulletin 140(6), 1432-1463 (g = 0.50); Adesope, O. O., Trevisan, D. A. & Sundararajan, N. (2017), Review of Educational Research 87(3), 659-701 (g = 0.61, 217 studies).
reported: Standardised retention advantage of retrieval practice over restudying (the testing effect), stronger for more complex material and more effortful retrieval, both of which describe this corpus.
model_quantity: NOT COMPUTED. M is a latent memory strength on [0, 1] that enters accuracy only through kappa * M in eq. 17, so eta_M has no direct expression as a standardised retention effect without a dedicated paired run (retrieval-heavy vs retrieval-light episodes at matched K). Recorded so Table 3 carries the source, with no consistency verdict claimed.

quantity: steady-state knowledge K* of eq. 21 at constant E and F
verdict: derived: the plateau the two rates imply together
model_detail: model gain 0.0346 vs delta 0.0244; literature midpoints gain 0.160 vs delta 0.00228 (from 0.70 retained per year)
source: derived from the two rows above
